method_card.title: Standard Deviation and Interpercentile Range
method_card.content:
Standard deviation and interpercentile range are Higher-tier spread measures that give more detailed information about how data are distributed around the mean.

The standard deviation measures the average distance of data values from the mean. A small standard deviation means values cluster tightly around the mean; a large standard deviation means they are more spread out. The formula is given in the question when you need to use it manually, but you are also permitted to use your calculator’s statistical functions (σ_n or σ_x button). The formula is: $$\sigma = \sqrt{\frac{\sum (x - \bar{x})^2}{n}}$$ An equivalent form for calculation is: $$\sigma = \sqrt{\frac{\sum x^2}{n} - \bar{x}^2}$$

The outlier rule using standard deviation: a value is an outlier if it is more than 3 standard deviations above or below the mean.

The interpercentile range (IPR) is the difference between two percentile values, e.g. the 90th minus the 10th percentile. The interdecile range (IDR) is the 90th minus the 10th percentile specifically. These are used when comparing the spread of distributions from cumulative frequency graphs.
steps: Find each deviation from the mean: \(x - \bar{x}\)
Sum the squared deviations and divide by \(n\): this gives the variance \(\sigma^2\)
Take the square root to get the standard deviation \(\sigma\)
Alternatively: use your calculator’s σ_n function directly after entering the data

exam_context.marks: 2–4 marks for a standard deviation calculation; 1–2 marks for interpreting a standard deviation in context
exam_context.frequency: Higher-only topic; appears on most Higher papers, often in comparison questions requiring interpretation alongside the mean

worked_examples.question: The formula for standard deviation is given as \(\sigma = \sqrt{\frac{\sum(x-\bar{x})^2}{n}}\). A dataset is: 2, 4, 6. The mean is 4. Calculate \(\sum(x-\bar{x})^2\).

steps.label: Step 1 — Find each deviation and square it

worked_examples.question: Using the formula \(\sigma = \sqrt{\frac{\sum(x-\bar{x})^2}{n}}\), calculate the standard deviation of: 3, 5, 7, 9, 11. Give your answer to 2 decimal places.

Two classes take the same test. Class A has mean 65 and standard deviation 3. Class B has mean 65 and standard deviation 12. A student in Class A scores 71, and a student in Class B scores 77. Which student performed better relative to their class? Use the formula \(z = \frac{x - \bar{x}}{\sigma}\) (given in the question).

steps.label: Step 2 — Interpret
steps.content: Class A student is 2.0 standard deviations above the mean. Class B student is 1.0 standard deviation above the mean.

steps.label: Answer
steps.content: The Class A student performed better relative to their class. A z-score of 2.0 means they scored further above the typical class performance (in standard deviation units) than the Class B student’s z-score of 1.0.

bronze.display: A dataset is: 5, 5, 5, 5, 5. Using the formula \(\sigma = \sqrt{\frac{\sum(x-\bar{x})^2}{n}}\), what is the standard deviation?

misconceptions.message: Mean = 5. Every deviation is 0. Sum of squared deviations = 0. Standard deviation = 0. When all values are equal, there is no spread.

bronze.display: The mean of a dataset is 10. One value is 14. What is \((x - \bar{x})^2\) for this value?

misconceptions.message: \((14 - 10)^2 = 4^2 = 16\). Squaring makes the result positive regardless of whether the deviation is positive or negative.

bronze.display: A dataset has \(\sum(x-\bar{x})^2 = 50\) and \(n = 5\). Using \(\sigma = \sqrt{\frac{\sum(x-\bar{x})^2}{n}}\), what is \(\sigma\) to 2 decimal places?

misconceptions.message: \(\sigma = \sqrt{50/5} = \sqrt{10} \approx 3.16\). Don't forget to divide before taking the square root.

bronze.display: A dataset has mean 20 and standard deviation 4. Which of the following values would be classified as an outlier using the '3 standard deviations' rule?

misconceptions.message: Upper boundary = mean + 3σ = 20 + 12 = 32. Lower boundary = 20 − 12 = 8. A value is an outlier if it is more than 3σ from the mean. 33 > 32, so 33 is an outlier. 30 is within bounds. 15 and 28 are also within bounds.

bronze.display: Two datasets both have mean 50. Dataset X has \(\sigma = 2\) and Dataset Y has \(\sigma = 15\). Which dataset is more spread out?
options: Dataset X, because it has a smaller standard deviation
Dataset Y, because it has a larger standard deviation
They are equally spread because they have the same mean
It is impossible to tell without knowing the number of values

misconceptions.message: A larger standard deviation means values are more spread out around the mean. Dataset Y (σ = 15) has greater spread than Dataset X (σ = 2).

bronze.display: Using the alternative formula \(\sigma = \sqrt{\frac{\sum x^2}{n} - \bar{x}^2}\) (given), a dataset has \(\frac{\sum x^2}{n} = 169\) and \(\bar{x} = 12\). Calculate \(\sigma\).
A cumulative frequency graph is used to find the 10th percentile (value = 18) and the 90th percentile (value = 62). What is the interdecile range?
A dataset is: 1, 3, 5, 7, 9. The mean is 5. Calculate \(\sum(x-\bar{x})^2\).

silver.display: Using \(\sigma = \sqrt{\frac{\sum(x-\bar{x})^2}{n}}\), calculate the standard deviation of: 4, 8, 6, 10, 2. Give your answer to 2 decimal places.
A dataset has mean 100 and standard deviation 8. Identify which value is more than 3 standard deviations from the mean.

misconceptions.message: Lower boundary = mean − 3σ = 100 − 24 = 76. Upper boundary = 124. A value must be MORE than 3σ from the mean to be an outlier. 73 < 76, so it is more than 3 standard deviations below the mean. The other options all fall within the boundaries.

silver.display: Using \(\sigma = \sqrt{\frac{\sum x^2}{n} - \bar{x}^2}\) (given), a dataset of 6 values has \(\sum x^2 = 580\) and mean 9. Calculate \(\sigma\) to 2 decimal places.
Class A exam scores: mean 70, σ = 5. Class B exam scores: mean 70, σ = 14. A student wants to join the class where scores are most consistent. Which class should they choose?
options: Class A, because its lower standard deviation means scores are more consistent
Class B, because a higher standard deviation allows for higher individual scores
Either class, because both have the same mean
Class B, because a larger spread gives more opportunity to stand out

misconceptions.message: Standard deviation measures spread around the mean. A smaller σ means values cluster more tightly around the average, indicating more consistent performance. Class A (σ = 5) is more consistent than Class B (σ = 14).

silver.display: A cumulative frequency graph shows the 25th percentile = 32 and the 75th percentile = 68. What is the interpercentile range between the 25th and 75th percentiles?

misconceptions.message: Interpercentile range = upper percentile value − lower percentile value = 68 − 32 = 36. Note: this is the same as the IQR (Q3 − Q1).

silver.display: A dataset of 5 values: 10, 12, 14, 16, 18. Calculate \(\sum x^2\).

gold.display: Two factories produce bolts. Factory A: mean length 50mm, σ = 0.5mm. Factory B: mean length 50mm, σ = 2mm. A bolt is rejected if it is more than 3 standard deviations from the mean. What is the rejection boundary (upper) for Factory B?
A dataset of 4 values has mean 8 and standard deviation 3. Using \(\sigma^2 = \frac{\sum(x-\bar{x})^2}{n}\) (given), what is \(\sum(x-\bar{x})^2\)?

A student in Group A scores 78 (group mean 70, σ = 4). A student in Group B scores 85 (group mean 72, σ = 9). Using \(z = \frac{x - \bar{x}}{\sigma}\) (given), which student performed better relative to their group?
options: Group A student (z = 2.0), because their z-score is higher
Group B student (z = 1.44), because they scored higher in absolute terms
Both performed equally because both scored above the mean
Group B student, because Group B has a higher mean

misconceptions.message: Group A: z = (78−70)/4 = 2.0. Group B: z = (85−72)/9 ≈ 1.44. A higher z-score means the student is further above their group's average in relative terms. Group A student performed better relative to their class.

gold.display: A dataset has n=6, \(\sum x = 60\), \(\sum x^2 = 700\). Using \(\sigma = \sqrt{\frac{\sum x^2}{n} - \bar{x}^2}\) (given), calculate \(\sigma\) to 2 decimal places.

Two distributions are compared from a cumulative frequency graph. Distribution P: 10th percentile = 15, 90th percentile = 45. Distribution Q: 10th percentile = 28, 90th percentile = 38. Which distribution is more spread out, and by how much (in terms of the interdecile range)?
options: P is more spread out; its IDR is 30 compared to Q’s IDR of 10
Q is more spread out; its IDR is 10 compared to P’s IDR of 30
P is more spread out; its IDR is 45 compared to Q’s IDR of 38

misconceptions.message: IDR = 90th − 10th percentile. P: 45 − 15 = 30. Q: 38 − 28 = 10. P has the larger IDR so P is more spread out.
